conviction_note: The print turns on the guide, and two things are already known from management: Ultra Mission Solutions will be rolled into guidance this month (it closed early, on 2026-08-24), and Q2 will show civil and margin pressure. FY EPS consensus of $6.31 already sits near the top of the $6.00-6.35 range, the stock rose 8.8% in five days (5.05% of that on 2026-10-22, the day after CACI raised its guide), and the 25-delta skew of +7.4 has buyers paying for downside. Each finding is small and they roughly offset to +0.6; abs_move 7.5 sits a little above the 6.89 implied move because this name moves on guidance updates. p_up 52 gives +0.3, so the two measurements agree.
bar: Q2 FY27 adj EPS consensus $1.44 (Unusual Whales/aggregator, https://unusualwhales.com/stock/BAH/earnings) vs $1.52 (Benzinga, https://it.benzinga.com/quote/BAH/earnings-forecasts); revenue $2.82B (Benzinga) vs ~$2.906B (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/news/BAH/Chartmill-51611-Booz-Allen-Hamilton-NYSEBAH-Delivers-Profitability-Surprise-Stock-Rises-on-Quality-Earnings-Beat). FY27 consensus $6.31 EPS / $11.41B revenue (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/BAH) against company guide of $6.00-6.35 / $11.2-11.7B (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001443646/000162828026049494/q1fy2027exhibit991_final.htm). The quarterly estimate sources disagree with each other, so quarter-level findings are capped small. The guide range is sourced to the company. Prior-year Q2 comparison: revenue $2.89B, adj EPS $1.49.
positioning_check: Short interest 6,895,199 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (about 5.7% of shares), 4.46 days to cover, falling from 9.08M on 2026-07-15 (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/bah/short-interest, read 2026-10-22). The next FINRA print is due 2026-10-26, after the window. This is not a crowded short, but it has been covering into the print. Baseline: 25-delta skew +7.37 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.38, event-implied move 6.89% (straddle 11.38% over 29 days; an aggregator quotes ±10.85%), 5-day run-up +8.83%, 20-day +3.39%, 23.5% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: On the Q1 FY27 call (2026-07-24) management said it would 'include into our guidance in October what's happening with Ultra'. Ultra I&C Mission Solutions ($720M, described as growing strong double digits with EBITDA margins well above 20%) closed on 2026-08-24, ahead of its Q2 target. So a mechanical lift to the FY27 revenue and EBITDA guide ($11.2-11.7B / $1.24-1.29B) is close to pre-announced. The EPS effect is muted by interest on the $1.2B of notes (5.375%/5.9%), of which about $714M refinanced existing loans.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on guidance. Q1 FY27 with the guide held after a profit beat: +10.11% (2026-07-24). Q2 FY26 guide cut (revenue to $11.3-11.5B from $12.0-12.5B): -8.86% (2025-10-24). FY26 initial guide: -16.53% (2025-05-23).
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced. A mechanical acquisition roll-in is something most holders expect, and FY EPS consensus of $6.31 near the top of the guide shows a raise is already assumed. What is not visible is the organic split: if Ultra lifts the reported range while organic revenue is cut (Q1 was -4.2% against a 0-4% FY range), the headline raise hides a cut. That uncertainty is why the size stays small.
findings.independence: Closing date from https://www.govconwire.com/articles/booz-allen-720m-ultra-ic-mission-solutions-close. Financing terms from https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20260728598351/booz-allen-hamilton-announces-pricing-of-senior-notes-offering. The October roll-in commitment itself has one source, the transcript.

findings.finding: The company told the market to expect a weak Q2: 'some pressure in 2Q on growth and profitability', civil revenue down double digits sequentially from Q1's $772M, and the margin stepping down from Q1's 11.9% toward about 11% for the year, 'particularly in 2Q'. My own arithmetic (civil about $690M, national security at about $2.05B plus roughly one month of Ultra) gives about $2.77B of revenue, against the $2.82B Benzinga consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 revenue slightly missed ($2.80B vs $2.81B) while EPS beat by $0.32, and the stock rose 10.1%, so a revenue shortfall was looked through. Q2 FY26 revenue missed by 3.1% alongside a guide cut: -8.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced, because the company guided to it and consensus EPS of $1.44-1.52 is well below Q1's $1.81. The only unpriced part is my own revenue arithmetic, which is an inference and depends on revenue estimates that disagree with each other.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the first finding. Q1 segment figures from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001443646/000162828026049494/q1fy2027exhibit991_final.htm.

findings.finding: CACI, the closest peer and the only one to report since BAH last spoke, posted fiscal Q1 FY27 on 2026-10-21 (quarter to 2026-09-30, the same calendar quarter as BAH's Q2): revenue +8.2% with 2.1% organic, Department of War revenue +14.8%, federal civilian -3.7%, funded backlog +14.8%, book-to-bill 2.0x, and FY27 revenue and EPS guidance raised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BAH rose 5.05% on 2026-10-22, the session after CACI's release (Equibles close $78.83), so the read-through has already moved this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the +5% day on 2026-10-22 is what pricing it looks like. What remains is that defense strength and only a modest civilian decline at CACI fit BAH's national-security ramp. CACI's civilian exposure is much smaller than BAH's, so the read-through on BAH's weak line is limited.
findings.independence: SAIC raised FY27 guidance on 2026-08-31 with 5.3% organic growth (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001571123/000157112326000131/saic08312026ex991earningsr.htm). This is a peer proxy, not BAH's own number.

findings.finding: There is no shutdown in this print's comparison or quarter. A continuing resolution funding the government at FY26 levels through 2026-12-11 was signed on 2026-09-02, whereas the Q2 FY26 print a year earlier carried an estimated $30M revenue / $15M profit shutdown hit and a guide cut. A new funding deadline (2026-12-11) falls inside H2 FY27, the half the guide is weighted toward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The October 2025 print, with a shutdown and a guide cut, fell 8.86%. In July management named a possible CR among four Congressional swing factors for the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro and mostly priced. The residual is that management can keep the guide without a funding-lapse haircut this time. The December deadline lets them stay cautious, which keeps the size small.
findings.independence: https://spacepolicyonline.com/news/house-clears-fy2027-cr-now-to-the-president/. The prior-year shutdown impact is from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1443646/000162828025046175/bahexhibit991q2fy26.htm. This is a macro-to-company link, so it is filed as a proxy.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print up 8.83% over five sessions (5.05% on 2026-10-22 alone) and up 18.9% from the pre-Q1 close of $65.87 to about $78.2. Meanwhile the option market pays +7.37 vol points for 25-delta puts over calls, and FY EPS consensus ($6.31) already sits at the top of the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Seven prints: 4 up and 3 down, median absolute move 6.76%. The last three prints went +6.76, +3.05 and +10.11, and the run-up now carries part of a good guide.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so the question is how high the bar now is. A raise only as large as the Ultra roll-in may not clear a stock that rose 5% in one session the day before. Short interest is moderate (4.5 days to cover) and falling, so there is no squeeze to offset a disappointment.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline records 5-day run-up +8.83% and skew +7.37. The Q1 price path is from https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-booz-allen-hamilton-stock-soared-today.

findings.finding: Management said in July it was 'a little bit behind' on hiring cleared staff because of supply constraints, and headcount fell to 30,900 from 33,400 year on year. The FY27 revenue guide of 0-4% growth needs national security to 'significantly ramp in the second half' after Q1 at -4.2% overall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Labor-driven revenue shortfalls led into the FY26 guide cuts (-16.5% in May 2025, -8.9% in October 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: The headcount decline is in the release, but the market priced the Q1 beat, not the second-half staffing math. If it had been priced, consensus FY revenue would sit below the $11.45B midpoint; it sits at $11.41B, close to it. Net of the rest of the company, funded backlog +15% and book-to-bill 1.5x support the ramp, so the finding stays small.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the first two findings. Headcount is from the 8-K exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001443646/000162828026049494/q1fy2027exhibit991_final.htm.

findings.finding: Q1 adjusted EPS of $1.81 came in $0.32 above the $1.49 consensus and up 22% year on year, and profit and cash were 'above expectations', yet the FY EPS guide of $6.00-6.35 was left unchanged ('this early in the year, we're not going to update guidance'). That leaves room to raise the EPS guide organically in October, not only through Ultra.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 profit beat with the guide held bought +10.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. FY consensus of $6.31 is $0.13 above the guide midpoint, so the street already assumes a raise toward the top. Only a raise above $6.35 at the top end would be news.
findings.independence: The Q1 consensus of $1.49 is from https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/BAH. This finding shares the guidance line with the first one but rests on a different fact (organic profit outperformance rather than the acquisition).

outside_window.finding: The FY27 continuing resolution expires on 2026-12-11. Full-year appropriations, or a lapse, decide the second-half funding the guide relies on.
The next FINRA short-interest settlement is published around 2026-10-26.

baseline_tension: The run-up and the downside-paid skew together say a good guide is largely in the price. My findings mostly agree that a raise is coming but are mostly already known, so they net to near zero instead of cutting clearly against the skew.
lessons_applied: Rule 6: the quarterly bar has two disagreeing sources ($1.44 vs $1.52 EPS; $2.82B vs $2.906B revenue) and Q2 weakness is inside what management guided, so the Q2-pressure finding went from -0.5 to -0.3
Rule 6: the hiring-constraint finding lands inside the guided range and is offset by funded backlog +15%, so it went from -0.5 to -0.4
Rule 5: the CR/no-shutdown finding is a macro-to-company link, so it went from +0.5 to +0.4

Rule 7: short interest checked (5.7% of shares, 4.46 days to cover, falling) and not crowded; the positioning negative agrees with the skew and went from -1.0 to -0.8 only because the run-up partly reflects a peer read-through that has some substance

Rule 1 and the line rule: the Q1-cushion EPS finding is mostly priced given FY consensus of $6.31, so it went from +0.5 to +0.4; the Ultra guidance finding stays at +1.0 because this name moves on guidance
